title: Pixel-art grass tile with tufts and flowers
purpose: Generate a tileable pixel-art grass tile at a chosen art resolution (16 to 64 pixels), enlarged with crisp nearest-neighbour pixels: dithered lawn patches, blade tufts, flowers and pebbles, with per-pixel normal, height, roughness and occlusion maps. Use for top-down and side-view 2D games.

contract.signature: generate(width=256, height=256, seed=0, preset="default", directx_normal=False, **parameters) -> {map name: {"channels", "colour_space", "pixels"}}
contract.command_line: python pixel_grass_tile.py --size 1024 --seed 7 --preset NAME --out DIR [--width W --height H] [--set NAME=VALUE] [--directx-normal] [--orm]

parameters.name: art_pixels
parameters.meaning: Art pixels along each side of the tile; the maps enlarge them with nearest-neighbour sampling.

parameters.name: blade_length
parameters.meaning: Typical blade length in art pixels.

parameters.name: patchiness
parameters.meaning: Contrast of the large light and dark patches of the lawn.

parameters.name: relief
parameters.meaning: Strength of the per-pixel normal map.

parameters.name: hue_shift
parameters.meaning: Hue rotation of the albedo in turns.

presets.name: default
presets.description: Lush green lawn with a few white and yellow flowers.

presets.name: dry_meadow
presets.description: Late-summer straw and olive grass, sparse tufts, a few pebbles.

presets.name: flower_meadow
presets.description: Dense meadow full of red, violet and white flowers.

presets.name: frosted
presets.description: Blue-grey frosted grass on a winter morning, short stiff blades.

limits: Stylized pixel art, not a physically based material: roughness and height are values per drawn class chosen for 2D lighting, and the normal map treats each art pixel as a flat facet. Tufts, flowers and pebbles are small fixed sprites, so a 16-pixel grid shows single-pixel flowers and fewer details. Output sizes that are not a whole multiple of art_pixels give art pixels of unequal widths. Occlusion is a blurred-height estimate posterized to eighths.
technique_references: Ordered dithering with a 4 x 4 Bayer matrix
Posterized fractal noise for lawn patch tones
Nearest-neighbour enlargement of an art grid
